confirmed_findings.summary: update_frontmatter_title replaces the root `title:` line but never consumes the key's BLOCK VALUE, so a note whose title is a block scalar (or whose value sits on the following indented lines) is left with orphaned indented lines under a now-scalar key — unparseable frontmatter, written to disk by the rename with no error.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario:
A note on disk reads:
```
---
title: >-
  A long two-line
  note title
tags: [x]
---
body
```
The user renames it in the sidebar. rename_item (libraries.rs:1658) calls gate_rmw_rename, whose closure calls extract_frontmatter_title (2146) — that returns `rest.trim()` of `title: >-`, i.e. the literal string ">-", as old_title. update_frontmatter_title then walks fm.lines(): line `title: >-` is a root key starting with `title:` so it is REPLACED by `title: "New"` and `continue`d (2254-2257); the two continuation lines `  A long two-line` / `  note title` are not root keys and not seq items, so they fall through to the catch-all push at 2302 and are re-emitted verbatim. The file is atomically written as:
```
---
title: "New"
  A long two-line
  note title
tags: [x]
aliases:
  - ">-"
---
```
That is invalid YAML (an indented scalar block after a plain scalar key). gate_rmw_rename journals WriteOutcome::Ok, rename_item returns Ok, the tree refreshes, no error surfaces anywhere. From then on the frontend's composeFrontmatter hits its invalid-YAML passthrough branch — the failure mode this file documents verbatim at 2233-2234 and 2349-2351 and 8906-8908 — so EVERY later property edit on that note is silently discarded while every save reports success. The old title is also permanently recorded as an alias literally named ">-", and the frontend cascade then walks the universe searching for `[[>-]]`.

The asymmetry is the proof this is an oversight rather than a decision: the sibling rewriter set_frontmatter_parent (2361-2383) replaces its key and explicitly consumes the old block value with yaml_lines::is_block_value_line, with a comment calling the orphaned-value outcome an APP-KILLER. update_frontmatter_title — the far more frequently executed of the two, on every rename — never got that half. The existing tests cover a block scalar under a DIFFERENT key (`desc: |`, test at 8881) and a nested `title:` under `source:` (8865), but none covers the note's OWN title being a block/multi-line value. search.rs:8046 ("a multi-line (block-scalar) title collapses to a single line for the display name") is the app's own evidence that such titles exist in real universes.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified at source. update_frontmatter_title (libraries.rs:2212-2303) replaces the root `title:` line and `continue`s without consuming the key's block value; a following indented continuation line is not a top-level key, not a seq item, and not inside the alias list, so it falls through to the catch-all push at 2302 and is re-emitted verbatim beneath a now-scalar key. I ran the project's own YAML parser on the emitted result: "All mapping items must start at the same column" + "Implicit map keys need to be followed by map values" — the frontmatter genuinely no longer parses. The path is unguarded end to end: rename_item (1658-1685) feeds fresh disk content straight in, gate_rmw_rename (714-730) atomic-writes it and journals WriteOutcome::Ok, and there is no YAML validation anywhere in the write path. extract_frontmatter_title (2146-2171) additionally returns the literal block indicator ("|" / ">-") as old_title, which is written into aliases and fed to the rename cascade. The asymmetry is real: the sibling set_frontmatter_parent (2361-2383) consumes the old block value via yaml_lines::is_block_value_line and its own comment calls the orphaned-value outcome an APP-KILLER; the far more frequently executed title rewriter never got that half, and no test covers the note's OWN title as a block value (8865 covers a nested source.title, 8881 covers `desc: |`, 8913/8956/8978 cover alias shapes). Reachability is established from the codebase itself rather than inferred: search.rs's test block_scalar_title_decodes_via_g4_reader writes `title: |` and its comment names "an Obsidian-imported multi-line title", and the indexer carries a dedicated branch collapsing a multi-line title for the display name; a folded plain scalar is equally reachable since standard YAML emitters fold a long title at ~80 columns. REFUTED PORTION: the candidate's tail claim that every later property edit is then silently discarded is outdated — PJ-207 §15 added frontmatterIsRewritable (yamlDoc.ts:419), noteModel.ts:163/179 sets base.rewritable, and propsAreWritable feeds propsCommit.apply's refused list into the PJ-187 PropertyEditor banner, so the later edit-loss IS surfaced. What remains silent is the corruption event itself: the rename writes unparseable frontmatter, mangles the note's real title into an orphan line, records an alias literally named "|", and reports success with no error, leaving the note permanently non-property-editable until hand-repaired. Bounded (frontmatter only, body intact, bytes recoverable by hand) and conditioned on a multi-line/block title, so HIGH rather than APP-KILLER.

confirmed_findings.summary: `moveItem` repaths the open tab and the note model but never refreshes `t.libraryName` / `t.libraryPath`, so after a cross-library move every subsequent save reindexes the note under its OLD library name, overwriting the correct attribution the Rust move-tail just wrote.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: Note `X.md` is open in a tab (tab.libraryName = "Library A"). User right-clicks → Move and picks a folder under "Library B" (MoveDialog's list comes from `list_universe_folders`, which enumerates every library root universe-wide; `handleMoveConfirm` at +layout.svelte:6993 even computes a `targetLibId` for the "possibly different" target library — cross-library moves are supported; the stale MoveDialog.svelte:4 comment claiming `move_item` rejects them is wrong, `move_item` only calls `validate_path_in_any_library` on both ends). `move_item_db_tail` (libraries.rs:2650) correctly reindexes the new path with `library_name_for_path` → note_meta.library_name = "Library B". The tab stays open; `openTabs.update` at store.ts:4991 returns `{ ...t, path: newPath, name: newName }` — libraryName untouched. The user then types one character. NotePane's 1500 ms debounce fires → NoteEditor.handleSave → `reindexNote(savedPath, tab.libraryName)` (NoteEditor.svelte:353) → `index_note(conn, newPath, "Library A")` → the UPSERT sets `library_name = excluded.library_name` and every re-INSERTed note_links row is stamped `library_name = "Library A"`. The note is now filed in the index under a library it does not live in: Library B's sidebar note count omits it, a library-scoped search/Sight/tag query in Library B misses it and a Library A query surfaces it. No error, no banner, no log — the save reports success and the .md is perfectly correct on disk. Nothing heals it: boot does not re-walk an indexed library, reconcile counts by PATH not by library_name, and the app's own write is watcher-suppressed. It persists until the user manually runs Settings → Index → Repair (which re-derives via `library_name_for_path`) or reopens the tab after a restart AND edits again (restoreTabsSession at store.ts:3771 uses `deriveLibraryForPath`, openNoteTab at store.ts:3440 uses `resolvedLibraryName` — both siblings resolve it correctly; `moveItem` is the one path that does not). Same stale value also feeds navFlushEnv (store.ts:653), the prop-save runPostSave (store.ts:1871) and commitFocusSave (+layout.svelte:1785). Fix: resolve via the existing `deriveLibraryForPath(newPath)` inside the moveItem tab update, exactly as `addLinkToNote` (store.ts:1505) was fixed for this same wrong-library-into-note_meta class by MIG-105 C7.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified at the site and along the whole path. moveItem (src/lib/libraries/store.ts:4988-4993) returns `{ ...t, path: newPath, name: newName }` and never refreshes `libraryName`/`libraryPath`. Cross-library moves are fully reachable: `list_universe_folders` (src-tauri/src/libraries.rs:2720) enumerates every library in the universe, `buildUniverseFolderEntries` (+layout.svelte:6891) offers them all, `move_item` (libraries.rs:2545) validates only `validate_path_in_any_library` on both ends (the MoveDialog.svelte:2 comment claiming rejection is stale), and handleMoveConfirm (+layout.svelte:6997) explicitly handles a "possibly different" target library. `move_item_db_tail` (libraries.rs:2654) attributes the new path correctly via `library_name_for_path`; the next save on the still-open tab then calls `reindexNote(savedPath, tab.libraryName)` (NoteEditor.svelte:353, plus store.ts:653/1871/3580/3662 and +layout.svelte:1795) and `index_note_impl` stamps `library_name = excluded.library_name` straight from the caller argument (search.rs:8168-8189) — Rust never re-derives on this path. The note_links diff treats the changed `o_lib == &library_name` as non-identical and re-INSERTs every edge with the wrong library (search.rs:8505-8582); sky_nodes inherits it via the note_meta trigger (search.rs:5738). No heal exists: boot reconcile's index_note is mtime-gated (`if !force … return Unchanged`, search.rs:7912-7922) and the save already advanced `modified`; DriftReport (reconcile.rs:83-113) is purely path/mtime based (drifted/missing_from_index/missing_on_disk/foreign_rows) so the PJ-207 drift notice cannot see attribution error and counts the row as `unchanged`; library_attribution_backfill is a one-off version-stamped pass (LIB_ATTR_VERSION = 1); and the watcher path that WOULD re-derive (`reindex_changed_paths` -> library_name_for_path, search.rs:13009) never sees the app's own write, which is suppressed in Rust (write_gate.rs:257 watcher_suppress::mark_with_parent) and again in the frontend (wasRecentlyWritten, 2 s, store.ts:1928). Consequences are user-visible but unannounced: sidebar library note counts aggregate note_meta.library_name (get_all_library_stats, libraries.rs:1147-1165), Search Hub's library filter is `library_name IN (...)` (search.rs:9582), and every Tension query is name-scoped (tension.rs:175/241/281/308) — so the destination library under-counts and misses the note while the source library surfaces it. The save reports success, the .md on disk is correct, no error/banner/log is raised. That moveItem is the outlier is proven by its siblings: loadTabHistoryEntry resolves via deriveLibraryForPath with the explicit comment "so cross-library history entries ... don't keep the old library's name/path on the tab" (store.ts:2060), openNoteTab uses resolvedLibraryName (store.ts:3286), restoreTabsSession uses deriveLibraryForPath (store.ts:3766). Fix is the one-line `deriveLibraryForPath(newPath)` inside the moveItem tab update. Not an app-killer — content is intact on disk and Settings -> Index -> Repair re-derives via library_name_for_path — but a concrete, silent, non-self-healing index divergence.

confirmed_findings.summary: A plain tab-strip switch cancels the outgoing editor's armed 1500 ms debounced save, and its teardown flush is then refused by NoteEditor's path-identity guard — so the outgoing note's unsaved edits are left in the in-memory model alone, with no disk write, no write-ahead net, and no re-armed timer, for an unbounded time.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: Note A is the active tab. The user types a paragraph; NotePane sets `dirty = true` and arms `debouncedSaveTimer` for 1500 ms (NotePane.svelte:594-595). Within that window the user clicks tab B in the tab strip (+layout.svelte:8582 → `switchTab`, store.ts:3901), which only does `activeTabId.set(tabId)` — unlike `openNoteTab` (store.ts:3409), `loadTabHistoryEntry` (:2046), `closeTab` (:3838) and the vacate path (:5179), it performs NO `flushOutgoing`. `$activeTab` flips to B, so NoteEditor's `{#key tab.id + '|' + tab.path + ...}` (NoteEditor.svelte:773) destroys NotePane-A. In `onDestroy`, line 1032 clears the pending debounce and line 1031 clears the 30 s idle interval; line 1043 calls `doFlush()`, which reaches `handleFlush(text, dirty=true, …, filePath = A.path)` — but NoteEditor is a single instance whose `tab` prop is already B, so `if (!filePath || filePath !== tab.path) return;` (NoteEditor.svelte:362) returns immediately. Nothing downstream runs: no `saveNoteSession`, and critically no `setWriteAhead` (NoteEditor.svelte:427), because that call sits past the guard. Model A stays dirty in the non-reactive `models` Map with `writeAheadBuffer`/localStorage holding nothing for A (the last successful save compare-and-cleared it via `clearWriteAheadIf`). No timer anywhere will fire for A again: the debounce is nulled, the idle interval is destroyed with the view, and `saveHealth`'s 10 s retry only covers already-FAILED writes. The tab strip shows no dirty indicator. If the process now dies non-gracefully (power loss, crash, taskkill, forced OS reboot) — i.e. anything that skips `flushAllForAppClose` (+layout.svelte:3277) — the paragraph is gone from disk, gone from the crash-recovery net, and there is no journal marker, no banner and no error. Nothing distinguishes it from a note that was never edited. The same guard also drops the flush's `ct.cursorPos`/`ct.scrollTop` write, so caret/scroll memory for A is lost on every switch.
confirmed_findings.reason: Chain verified end-to-end in source; this is the still-unfixed PJ-086. (1) switchTab (store.ts:3901-3907) is the ONLY note-editing departure with no flushOutgoing — its whole body is activeTabId.set/focusedTabId.set, while openNoteTab (:3409), loadTabHistoryEntry (:2046), closeTab (:3838) and the vacate sweep (:5179) all flush. (2) Non-split mode mounts a single NoteEditor with tab={$activeTab} (+layout.svelte:9383) keyed on tab.id|tab.path|reloadVersion (NoteEditor.svelte:773), so the click destroys NotePane-A. (3) NotePane.onDestroy (:1030-1046) clears the armed 1500 ms debounce AND the 30 s idle interval, then doFlush() passes mountedFilePath = A (:359,:372). (4) handleFlush returns at `filePath !== tab.path` (NoteEditor.svelte:362) because `tab` is a live $props() binding already pointing at B — an ordering the repo asserts as OBSERVED in two independent APP-KILLER post-mortems (NotePane.svelte:350-358 "during the {#key}-triggered destroy filePath already points to the NEW tab"; PropertyEditor.svelte:75-83). setWriteAhead sits at :427, below that guard, so no recovery copy is stashed. (5) No other net exists: setBody (noteModel.ts:248) never touches the net; captureSessionSnapshot (session.ts:94-119) deliberately excludes content; the only setWriteAhead sites are the two in handleFlush, the cascade refusal (store.ts:711) and three openNoteTab restash points; saveHealth's 10 s retry covers only already-FAILED writes; and an exhaustive sweep of every writeNote(/saveNoteSession( call site shows no periodic writer. (6) The tab strip (+layout.svelte:8574-8595) draws pin/library/maturity/title/close only — no dirty indicator. Net effect: type in A, click tab B inside the debounce, and A's edits (up to ~30 s of continuous typing since the last idle-save tick) live ONLY in the non-reactive model Map, for unbounded time, with no disk write, no write-ahead entry, no journal marker, no banner and no re-armed timer. Graceful close is covered (flushAllForAppClose, +layout.svelte:3277) and returning to A and typing re-arms the debounce, so this is not APP-KILLER — but any non-graceful exit (crash, power loss, taskkill, OS shutdown = the still-open PJ-112) loses it indistinguishably from a note that was never edited. Same guard also drops ct.cursorPos/ct.scrollTop (NoteEditor.svelte:385-390), so caret/scroll memory is lost on every plain switch. Counter-evidence weighed and does not refute: the 2026-07-16 PJ-103 live arc reported 2/2 plain switches persisting, but the timing was never instrumented and no code path other than the already-cleared debounce/idle timers can write A after a switch — so those markers were written BEFORE the teardown, not by it; that arc's own conclusion left PJ-086 open as "re-examine", not closed. Per Reproduce-First, the fix (wire flushOutgoing into switchTab, or make the teardown stash to the net before the identity refusal) should still be preceded by an instrumented repro that timestamps the last keystroke vs the click.

confirmed_findings.summary: `sky_links` — the edge table Sky View draws from — has NO repair path anywhere in the codebase: its only bulk populator is a stamp-gated, INSERT-OR-IGNORE-only pass that can add missing rows but never remove wrong ones, `recompute_all_sky` touches only `sky_nodes` columns, and `index_note`'s no-op fast path stops an ordinary re-save from re-firing the mirror triggers.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: Take the divergence the codebase itself measured. Until 2026-08-09 the `note_meta_sky_au` rename trigger rewrote `sky_links.target_name` keyed on NAME alone; on the Boss's universe, retitling one of seven notes titled "Doi" rewrote 4,359 rows, ~4,300 of which belong to the other six notes and whose `[[...]]` on disk was never touched (`search.rs:5760-5785` records this verbatim). The statement was deleted, and the same comment states the already-diverged rows "need the reconciliation pass". No such pass exists, and each of the four candidates is provably incapable: (1) `sky_backfill::is_needed` (sky_backfill.rs:88-97) returns true only when `schema_versions.sky < SKY_SCHEMA_VERSION` — it never probes for missing or orphan rows, unlike its sibling `target_base_backfill::needs_run` (target_base_backfill.rs:68-87) which explicitly re-arms behind its own stamp when a NULL row exists; (2) even if the stamp were bumped, the repopulator is `INSERT OR IGNORE INTO sky_links ... SELECT ... FROM note_links` (sky_backfill.rs:286-291) — purely additive, so a row pointing at the wrong `target_name` survives every re-run; (3) `links_backfill::recompute_all_sky` (links_backfill.rs:371-402) only issues `UPDATE sky_nodes SET stratum/maturity`, which `index_repair.rs:415` states in terms ("nothing in the codebase rebuilds `sky_links` — `recompute_all_sky` only UPDATEs `sky_nodes` columns"); (4) re-saving either endpoint does not heal it, because `index_note`'s `unchanged` fast path (search.rs:8503-8517) skips the entire `note_links` DELETE/INSERT block when the parsed edge set matches what is stored, so `note_links_sky_ad`/`_ai` never fire. Net effect on the live universe today: Sky View draws ~4,300 edges into nodes that do not own them and omits ~4,300 real ones, permanently, while `note_links` (the actual index of the `.md` wikilinks) says the opposite — with no error, no drift notice, and no user-reachable remedy, since "Repair index" runs `converge`, whose five families do not include `sky_links`.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified in code AND measured live on the Boss's real index. (1) Reachability is not hypothetical: querying E:\Constellation Universes\Eisa Cognitive Knowledge\.constellation\search.db (last written 2026-08-10, i.e. AFTER the 2026-08-09 trigger deletion) read-only shows 4,371 sky_links rows with no matching note_links row (4,359 of them pointing at 'doi (identifier) test') and 4,333 active note_links rows with no sky_links row — 16 of which are the structural parent/contains lane excluded by design, leaving 4,317 genuinely missing cognitive edges (4,308 targeting 'doi (identifier)'). Exactly the predicted shape, ~1.9% of the 234,935 sky edges, still present today. (2) Every refutation avenue is closed by the actual code: sky_backfill::is_needed (sky_backfill.rs:89-98) gates on `stored_version < SKY_SCHEMA_VERSION` alone with no completeness probe — unlike its sibling target_base_backfill::needs_run (target_base_backfill.rs:68-88), which re-arms behind its own stamp via a NULL probe (Needs::Rearm); even if re-armed, the repopulator is `INSERT OR IGNORE INTO sky_links … SELECT … FROM note_links` (sky_backfill.rs:284-295), purely additive, so a wrong row survives every re-run. converge's sky family (converge.rs:297) is links_backfill::recompute_all_sky (links_backfill.rs:371-403), which issues only `UPDATE sky_nodes SET stratum, maturity` — index_repair.rs:415 states this in terms — so both "Repair index" scopes (Full and Full re-read) leave sky_links untouched. index_note's `unchanged` fast path (search.rs:8505-8518) and per-edge `identical` skip (8544-8555) leave unmodified edges' rows alone, so note_links_sky_ai/_ad/_au never re-fire on an ordinary re-save or a forced re-read (force only bypasses the mtime gate, search.rs:7912); only de-indexing the note (search.rs:12474-12477 → note_meta_sky_ad's `DELETE FROM sky_links WHERE source_path = OLD.path`) clears a source's rows. (3) It is silent: converge.rs:410 states the drift check "compares `.md` files to the index and cannot see a derived table stale against itself" — no error, no drift notice, no receipt. (4) It is unfiled: the code comment at search.rs:5775 declares the diverged rows "need the reconciliation pass", but grepping docs/Constellation Pending Jobs v1.79.md finds only the forward-fix recorded — no PJ exists for the residue. Net: Sky View / GraphMind permanently draw 4,359 edges into a node that does not own them and omit 4,317 real ones, while note_links (the faithful index of the wikilinks on disk) says the opposite, with no signal and no remedy.

confirmed_findings.summary: `listItemsOf`'s scalar fallback splits on a raw comma (`String(p.value).split(',')`) instead of the quote-aware `splitFlowSeqItems` that `parseFrontmatter` uses for the identical job — so a quoted value containing a comma is torn into two items on the way into the panel, and written back to disk as two items.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: A note has `parent: "[[Ibn Khaldūn, A Study]]"` — the exact shape Constellation's own `set_frontmatter_parent` writes, and the shape `src-tauri/src/yaml_lines.rs:229` names as "the case that destroys a link". `parseFrontmatter` (store.ts:2737-2754) unquotes it, `detectPropertyType` matches `/^\[\[.*\]\]$/` at store.ts:216 and returns `link`, so `listItems` is left undefined. PropertyEditor's seed forces `shownType = 'list'` for `parent`/`contains` (PropertyEditor.svelte:472) and derives the items via `listItemsOf` (PropertyEditor.svelte:483), which returns `['[[Ibn Khaldūn', 'A Study]]']` (verified by running). The panel draws TWO chips, 'Ibn Khaldūn' and 'A Study'. The user clicks the × on the second — `removeTag` (PropertyEditor.svelte:817) reads the same broken items — and the commit sets `type:'list', listItems:['[[Ibn Khaldūn']`. `composeFrontmatter` splices the scalar item and `serializeLine` emits `parent:\n  - "[[Ibn Khaldūn"` (verified by running `yaml.stringify`). The structural parent link is gone from the .md, the frontmatter re-parses cleanly as a one-item list, the reindex faithfully mirrors the broken value, and nothing is reported. store.ts:2750/2766-2772 already fixed exactly this by routing to `splitFlowSeqItems`; the mutator/renderer half in propRow was never swept. `+layout.svelte:7020`'s `addTagToProps` carries a seventh, equally naive copy of the same fallback.
confirmed_findings.reason: Real, reachable, silent on-disk corruption. Verified by reading the whole chain and by running the actual serializer. (1) src-tauri/src/libraries.rs:2329 writes `parent: \"[[{name}]]\"` verbatim, so a note title containing a comma produces `parent: \"[[Ibn Khaldūn, A Study]]\"` — Constellation's own output. (2) The panel's rows come from the model (PropertyEditor.svelte:184-188), whose props are projectProps (yamlDoc.ts:224-240): shape 'scalar' → {value:'[[Ibn Khaldūn, A Study]]', type:'text', listItems: undefined}; the `?? properties` fallback (store.parseFrontmatter) gives the same row typed 'link' (store.ts:216) with listItems undefined. (3) The seed (PropertyEditor.svelte:467-490) forces shownType='list' for parent/contains (line 165-167) and derives items via listItemsOf, whose scalar fallback (propRow.ts:101) splits on a raw comma → ['[[Ibn Khaldūn','A Study]]']; two chips render (line 1308-1316). (4) Any ordinary edit on that key — removeTag (817) or addTag (805) — reads the same torn array and commits type:'list' with those items; setPropValue accepts (noteModel.ts:342-351) and composeFrontmatter takes the splice-and-append branch (yamlDoc.ts:548-556, since np.type==='list' is excluded from the in-place scalar path). (5) Confirmed by running the real `yaml` library: removing the second chip emits `parent:\n  - \"[[Ibn Khaldūn\"\n`; adding a parent emits three items, two of them broken halves. The structural parent link is destroyed on disk, the result re-parses with ZERO errors (so no H1 refusal, no PJ-187 refusal banner, no console error), and the reindex mirrors the broken value — nothing anywhere reports a discrepancy. Refutations attempted and defeated: the PJ-207 §15 seed-baseline (line 492) prevents only the unasked open-time rewrite, not a genuine user edit; samePropRow protects only untouched keys; propsAreWritable/H1 never fire because the YAML parses cleanly before and after; seqCarryingComments is bypassed (a scalar key has no origSeq); no write-path validation of wikilinks exists. Blast radius extends past `parent`/`contains` to any key the library type-registry shows as List whose value is a comma-bearing scalar (e.g. `author: \"Rosenthal, F.\"`), via the same listItemsOf call at line 484, plus the seventh naive copy at +layout.svelte:7020. ONE CORRECTION to the candidate's remediation (does not change the verdict): routing to splitFlowSeqItems would NOT fix it — by the time the value reaches listItemsOf the quotes are already stripped (projectProps returns the decoded scalar; store.parseFrontmatter calls unquote first), so the quote-aware scanner sees `[[Ibn Khaldūn, A Study]]` with no quotes and splits it identically. store.ts:2737 needed a separate `wasQuoted` flag for exactly this reason. The fix must carry 'these items came from a scalar, not a flow sequence' into the row (or refuse to split a quoted/wikilink-shaped scalar), at propRow.ts:98-101 and the +layout.svelte:7020 copy.

confirmed_findings.summary: `open_existing_universe` flips the active-universe pointer without calling `invalidate_search_state` / `invalidate_libraries_cache`, and because `SearchState.db_ready` is an unkeyed boolean, the search connection is never re-opened for the newly-active universe for the rest of the process.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: Universe A is open and fully booted, so `state.db` holds A's `search.db`, `db_ready == true` (search.rs:1363), and `ensure_search_db_ready` returns Ok from the lock-free fast path at search.rs:11483 without ever consulting a path. The user opens the Universe Manager and clicks "Open existing", picking universe B's folder (UniverseManager.svelte:142 → `openExistingUniverse`). The already-registered branch at universe.rs:1244-1248 does `*lock = Some(canon)` and returns; the fresh-registration branch at universe.rs:1310-1311 does the same. Neither calls `crate::search::invalidate_search_state(&app)` — the call `set_active_universe` makes at universe.rs:1057 precisely so "the next `ensure_search_db_ready` opens the DB at the NEW universe's path" — and the frontend handler calls only `refresh()`, never `onSwitch`/`onBeforeSwitch`. From this instant the process is split-brained and stays that way until restart: `db_path()` (search.rs:1465-1468) resolves to B/.constellation/search.db, while every read and write that goes through `state.db` is served by A's database, with `ensure_search_db_ready` reporting Ok to all of them. Nothing is logged and no error is returned. Concretely: the user then runs Settings → Index → repair; the worker calls `ensure_search_db_ready` (Ok, A's stale conn) at index_repair.rs:594 and `reconcile_filesystem` opens its own connection at `db_path` = B (search.rs:11972-11977), drops and recreates B's outgoing-link triggers, walks, writes and stamps B — then emits a success receipt into a UI that is reading A. Universe B's search.db is rewritten by a repair the user believed applied to what was on screen, and A's index is left exactly as drifted as before, with a green receipt saying otherwise. The same unkeyed-readiness hole exists at universe.rs:1431 (`link_library_as_universe`) and universe.rs:2038 (`migrate_legacy_data`), which are setup-only surfaces.

confirmed_findings.summary: merge_initial_frontmatter drops a filtered top-level identity key line but keeps that key's indented continuation / block-value lines, so a template whose title:/kind:/created:/cid_cn: carries a multi-line or nested value produces a new note whose frontmatter is invalid YAML from birth.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario:
A user's template file in the Templates folder carries:
```
title: >
  Weekly review for
  the current cycle
stage: seed
```
The user creates a note from it. create_note (1256) calls merge_initial_frontmatter(extra) at 1289. The loop at 1223: `title: >` is a top-level key line whose trimmed form starts with `title:` → `continue` (1247), so the key is correctly dropped. cid_cn: 20260811T...
kind: note

The same shape fires for a `kind:` or `created:` key holding a nested map or block sequence; the PJ-182 comment at 1228-1232 shows this exact family (a filtered key holding a zero-indent block) has already bitten once, and the fix applied there (excluding seq items from is_top_level_key_line) does not change the outcome for the value lines — they were pushed before that change and are pushed after it.
confirmed_findings.reason: CONFIRMED by code read + empirical parse. merge_initial_frontmatter (libraries.rs:1221-1253) drops a filtered top-level identity key line but has NO block-value skip: any following indented line or `- ` item fails is_top_level_key_line (yaml_lines.rs:190) and is pushed verbatim at 1250, landing directly under the app-stamped `created: <rfc3339>` (1286). confirmed_findings.summary: After a commit the panel re-seeds `seededRows` from the UNTRANSFORMED model props while `editableProps` still hold the display-transformed rows, so on the next commit every transformed-but-untouched key is falsely reported as 'the user edited this' and gets rewritten on disk unasked.

[])` takes the model's RAW props, which for any key the commit did not touch still carry the pre-transform `type`/`listItems`. Semantic damage: the log exists to distinguish what the classifier got wrong; this inverts every dual-axis confirmation into a correction of a blank prediction, destroying exactly that signal on the vertical axis while the horizontal line beside it is correct. Fix must thread the pre-write snapshot into the second axis (parameters, or move logging to the dual-axis cece_record_correction_for_card seam); patching only mod.rs:1287 leaves classifier/mod.rs:430/:435 broken.

confirmed_findings.summary: FocusPane's durable save path (`commitFocusSave`) reindexes FTS but never calls `reembedNote`, so a note whose body is written in Focus mode keeps its PRE-edit semantic vector forever — the exact swallowed-embed class PJ-207 §15 closed at the four NotePane/nav/prop save sites, with the Focus surface missed.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: Semantic search is enabled and note N already has a `note_embeddings` row (created by the boot backfill or an earlier NotePane save). The user opens N, enters Focus mode, and types the entire body there — Focus is the capture surface, so this is its normal use. After 1500 ms `commitFocusSave` (+layout.svelte:1780-1796) composes the model, writes the .md durably through `saveNoteSession`, and its `onSaved` runs exactly two side effects: `broadcastNoteSaved` and `reindexNote` (line 1795). `reembedNote` — the choke point store.ts:4143 that owns the semanticSearch gate, the bounded retry and the `embedHealthError` surface — is never called; grep confirms only four call sites exist (NoteEditor.svelte:329, :445, store.ts:660 navFlushEnv, store.ts:1875 prop-save), none of them on this path. Nothing self-corrects it: `constellation_embed_notes` (embeddings.rs:451) skips any path that already has a row unless `force` is passed, `constellation_search_reindex` does not re-embed, and index_repair never touches `note_embeddings`. The user exits Focus and closes the tab; the model is clean so NotePane's save never fires. From then on lexical search finds the new text while semantic search, "similar notes" and CECE keep answering from the note's pre-Focus content — permanently, with no banner, no log the release build can show, and no way for the user to tell. Same omission at store.ts:6167 (merge_resolve, a wholesale body replacement) and store.ts:528 (retry_save, the recovery path for a body that failed to write).

confirmed_findings.summary: `reportExternalConflict` swallows a failed `write_conflict_sidecar` into a console.error, and because `reportConflict` (the banner) sits INSIDE the try after the await, a failed sidecar write means the user is never told an external edit arrived at all — the incoming disk copy is discarded and the dirty model's next autosave overwrites it.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: Note N is open with unsaved edits (dirty model). Syncthing/Git/Obsidian/another device rewrites N.md on disk. The watcher fires; `adoptExternalChangeIntoTabs` (store.ts:1350) sees dirty + `diskDiffersFromBaseline` and routes N to the conflict hook, which is `reportExternalConflict` — the one mechanism whose stated contract is that the external edit is "never lost" (store.ts:470). `write_conflict_sidecar` (libraries.rs:947) then fails: it appends ~28 chars (`.conflict-YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ.md.txt`) to the note's stem, so on Windows a long title in a deep Universe folder overflows MAX_PATH; a full disk, a read-only/synced folder, or an AV lock on `gate_create_exclusive` do the same. The rejection lands at line 479 in a `catch` that only calls `console.error` — invisible in a release build (devtools disabled, `feedback_devtools_dev_only`), and because `reportConflict(sidecarPath, …)` is the line ABOVE the catch it never runs, so no row is added to `saveConflicts` and NO conflict banner appears. On screen the note looks untouched and still dirty; nothing indicates an external change occurred. The next 1500 ms autosave composes from the model and writes it over N.md through the gate, and the external writer's version is gone from disk, from the sidecar, and from the UI. Reachable from all seven `{ conflict: reportExternalConflict }` call sites, including the rename-cascade reload (+layout.svelte:7500) and the watcher path (+layout.svelte:1747).
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified in source. store.ts:474-481: `reportConflict(...)` sits INSIDE the try after `await invoke('write_conflict_sidecar')`, so a rejected sidecar write falls to a bare `console.error` (line 479) and no `saveConflicts` row is ever added — no banner, no toast, nothing on screen (devtools are disabled in release per feedback_devtools_dev_only). The incoming disk content is retained nowhere else: in `adoptExternalChangeIntoTabs` (store.ts:1350-1356, 1389-1392) the dirty branch's `disk` string is passed only to this hook, the model refuses to adopt (dirty), and the write-ahead net is cleared for adopters only (line 1379), so the refuser keeps its own net, not the remote copy. The Rust command (libraries.rs:948-966) propagates `gate_create_exclusive`/`atomic_write` failures as Err → a JS rejection, reachable on a read-only or Controlled-Folder-Access-protected directory, disk-full, a removed network/removable volume, or an AV lock on the temp create/rename. Nothing stops the follow-up overwrite: `writeNote` (store.ts:2906) passes no `expect`; gate_write's self-attestation compares only cid_cn (same note → SelfAttestedOk) and `WRITE_GATE_ENFORCE = false` means even a WouldRefuseStale verdict still writes (write_gate.rs:435-441); `atomic_write` keeps no backup. The conflict branch fires only while the model is dirty, i.e. a 1500 ms debounced save is already pending, so the external writer's version is overwritten within ~1.5 s and is gone from disk, from any sidecar, and from the UI — the user is never told an external edit arrived at all. All seven `{ conflict: reportExternalConflict }` call sites share the path. The same codebase already fixed this exact pattern on the focus-save path (+layout.svelte:1755-1757: "replaced the console-only log, which is invisible in a release build"), and the fix here is one line — move `reportConflict` out of the try / report a conflict-without-copy row. Severity MED rather than HIGH: the loss is silent and real, but it is gated behind an independent I/O failure, the user's own unsaved work is preserved (adoptDisk refuses on dirty), the note is not corrupted, and in the Syncthing/Git origins the lost version usually still exists on the writing device; the unconditional half of the defect is the suppressed conflict notice.

confirmed_findings.summary: `record_change` returns early when `state.db` is None and `record_shape_change` then returns `Ok(())`, so a shape set during the cold-boot init window is written to the .md but its history row — which exists nowhere but search.db — is silently never created.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: `record_change` bails at shape.rs:238-239 (`let Ok(guard) = state.db.lock() else { return }; let Some(conn) = guard.as_ref() else { return };`) and its caller `record_shape_change` (shape.rs:323-343) unconditionally returns `Ok(())`; the command never calls `ensure_search_db_ready`, so it does not even try to install the connection. During the documented 20-40 s cold init on a large universe (search.rs:11366-11367) the editor is already painted and interactive, so the user can shape a note: NoteEditor.svelte:605 fires `record_shape_change` and the promise RESOLVES, the shape key lands durably in the note's frontmatter via the model's own save, and no `shape_history` row is written. `shape_history` has no on-disk source — it is search.db-only — so the step is unrecoverable. The user then presses undo/revert and gets "Nothing to undo for this note." (shape.rs:378) or "No shape history for this note yet." (shape.rs:308), which is indistinguishable from having never shaped it. Even a genuine rejection would be invisible: the only handler is `console.error` (NoteEditor.svelte:609) and release builds disable devtools.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified by reading the code, not inferred. (1) shape.rs:238-239 `record_change` returns early when `state.db` holds None, and its caller `record_shape_change` (shape.rs:323-343) returns Ok(()) unconditionally — neither calls `ensure_search_db_ready`, so the command never even attempts to install the connection. (2) The None window is real and in-repo-documented: `state.db` is published only at search.rs:11632 (`*db = Some(conn)`) AFTER `init_db_scoped` (search.rs:4601+, which can drop and FTS5-`rebuild` a multi-GB index), and cache.rs:166-170 / 1542-1546 both state this is "the whole 20-40s cold init after a universe switch / boot" — the stated reason those commands were made `(async)`. (3) The window is reachable with a live UI: +layout.svelte:2626 sets `appReady = true` as the first statement of `initializeApp`, libraries are loaded by 2884, and `await refreshLibraryCaches()` → `cache_boot_snapshot_core` → `ensure_search_db_ready` (cache.rs:185) is only awaited at 2919; opening a note in between needs no DB (`libraries::read_note`, libraries.rs:852-859, is a bare fs::read_to_string). (4) The control is ungated — NotePane.svelte:1598-1616 renders Scrap/Page/Clear/Revert behind only `{#if !readOnly}`. (5) Both write branches lose the row: the model branch (NoteEditor.svelte:604-609) and the no-model branch (591 → set_note_shape → apply_shape → same record_change); the shape key itself lands durably either way. (6) Nothing repairs it — grepping `shape_history` across src-tauri shows it is only written by record_change, path-rewritten on move (libraries.rs:1545-46), deleted on note-delete (search.rs:12523) and exported; there is no disk source and no reconstruction/backfill. (7) The consequence is silent: undo_shape's rejection is deliberately swallowed as an expected end state (NoteEditor.svelte:737-742, console.error only; release builds disable devtools), so Revert becomes a dead control, or — with an earlier surviving row — walks back to a stale shape. No refutation avenue holds: the write is not durable elsewhere, no guard/version-gate/trigger/reconcile covers it, the path is reachable, and it does not self-correct visibly. Held at MED rather than higher because no note content or index diverges — apply_shape touches only the `shape` frontmatter key, the shape is durable on disk, and the user can restore any state from the same menu; the unrecoverable casualty is one undo step of a three-state presentation attribute. Not LOW because it is the same silently-inert-Revert failure shape the Boss reported on 2026-07-20 and that this exact code was hardened against.

confirmed_findings.summary: The per-note Backlinks/Outgoing effect never clears `currentBacklinks`/`currentOutgoing` on a note CHANGE (only when there is no tab at all), so the PREVIOUS note's link rows stay rendered while `activeNoteName`/`activeNotePath` already point at the NEW note — and both panels build their confidence/archive menu by pairing a ROW with the ACTIVE note, so a right-click in that window writes the earned-link decision onto the wrong (source, target) pair.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: Note A is open with the right sidebar on the Backlinks tab; A has backlinks from note S. The user clicks note B in the file tree. The effect at +layout.svelte:1911 runs, sets `perNoteLinksLoading = true` (line 1931) and schedules the fetch (0 ms on a settled switch, 180 ms during a burst, plus the `get_backlink_rows` + `get_outgoing_rows` round-trip). It does NOT clear `currentBacklinks`/`currentOutgoing` — only the `if (!tab)` branch does. BacklinksPanel renders rows before it renders the loading state (`{#if showLinked && filteredBacklinks.length > 0}` precedes `{:else if showLinked && loading}`, BacklinksPanel.svelte:296-301), so A's rows are on screen and clickable. In that window the user right-clicks one of A's backlink rows: BacklinksPanel.svelte:204 calls `openConfMenu(e, bl.path /* = S, from A's stale row */, activeNoteName /* = B, already switched */, …)`, and the mirrored OutgoingLinksPanel.svelte:167 calls `openConfMenu(e, activeNotePath /* = B */, link.target /* from A's stale row */, …)`. The captured pair is frozen into `confMenu`, so the user can pick from the popover seconds later. Picking 'Archive' calls `archiveLink(S, B)` → `constellation_link_archive` (search.rs:10931), which (a) appends a PERMANENT `retire_line(src_cid, tgt_cid, …)` decision to the durable link-life ledger BEFORE touching the DB (search.rs:10950), and (b) runs `UPDATE note_links SET status='archived', weight=0.0 WHERE source_path=?1 AND LOWER(target_name)=?2` and returns `Ok(())` regardless of rows affected. Two silent outcomes: if S does link to B (ordinary in a hub-linked universe) the user has just archived a link they never selected — archived status lives ONLY in search.db (CLAUDE.md: not recomputable from the .md), and `link_life_restore` replays the ledger line on every boot, so it is re-applied forever; if S does not link to B the UPDATE matches zero rows and the command still resolves Ok, so the confidence/archive the user believed they set on S→A never happened and nothing surfaces. Either way the panel then re-fetches for B, so the rows the user acted on disappear and no surface reports anything. The identical seam in the SAME component was confirmed and fixed for the UNLINKED-MENTIONS rows on 2026-08-01 (`_unlinkedRowsForPath`, +layout.svelte:1982-2003, whose comment states this exact reasoning); the linked-backlink and outgoing rows never got the equivalent per-path clear.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified end to end in source. (1) The stale window is real and unguarded: the per-note effect at +layout.svelte:1911 clears currentBacklinks/currentOutgoing ONLY in the `if (!tab)` branch (1915-1921); on a note CHANGE it sets perNoteLinksLoading=true (1931) and leaves the previous note's rows in place. The legacy branch (1849-1856) has the same shape. (2) The stale rows are visibly rendered with no cue: BacklinksPanel.svelte:288 `{#if showLinked && filteredBacklinks.length > 0}` precedes `{:else if showLinked && loading}` (300), and OutgoingLinksPanel.svelte:200 precedes :212 — so rows always beat the loading state. No `{#key}` wraps either mount (9331, 9508, 9771, 9785); nothing remounts or resets them. (3) The mispairing is real: BacklinksPanel.svelte:204 pairs `bl.path` (stale row) with `activeNoteName`, and OutgoingLinksPanel.svelte:167 pairs `activeNotePath` with `link.target` (stale row); both active props come from the same sidebarTab/$activeTab that has ALREADY switched (9776-9777, 9788-9789). The pair is frozen into confMenu (BacklinksPanel:81), so only the right-click needs to land in the window — the pick can come seconds later. (4) The write is durable and silent: constellation_link_archive (search.rs:10931) appends a PERMANENT retire_line to the earned ledger before touching the DB (10950), then runs the UPDATE with NO rows-affected check and returns Ok(()) (10958-10975); constellation_link_set_confidence (10833) is identical. link_life.rs:361 folds `retire` -> status='archived' on the cid pair and replays it on every load, so a wrong-pair retire is permanent. ConfidencePicker.svelte:63-86 surfaces only a Rust Err — a 0-row Ok(()) closes the menu as success, and applyArchiveLocally/applyConfidenceLocally (+layout.svelte:919/935) bump the nonce so the acted-on row disappears in the refetch. (5) The window is not merely tens of ms: get_backlink_rows (cache.rs:636) routes through with_read_conn, which holds the single read_db mutex for the ENTIRE closure (search.rs:1492-1507) — a hazard the repo documents twice (target_base_backfill.rs:154 "would then block every other read at boot for seconds", measured 2,606 ms first-use; cece/wiring.rs:151-158, the Cataloger's brute-force kNN scanning every embedding inside with_read_conn for an hour-long job). Under any such holder each note switch leaves the prior note's rows on screen for hundreds of ms to seconds. Both silent outcomes follow: if S->B exists, an archive/confidence the user never selected lands durably in the ledger + search.db (per CLAUDE.md the ONLY record of earned link state, not recomputable from the .md); if it does not, the UPDATE matches zero rows, the command still resolves Ok, the menu closes as success, and the user's decision silently evaporated. The identical seam was CONFIRMED and fixed for the unlinked-mentions rows in the same file on 2026-08-01 (_unlinkedRowsForPath, +layout.svelte:1973-1991, whose comment states this exact reasoning) — the linked-backlink and outgoing arrays never received the equivalent per-path clear. Not an app-killer (scope is one link decision, .md files untouched, requires a right-click inside the window), but a real silent divergence/false-success on the system of record for earned link data.

confirmed_findings.summary: discover_template_shapes runs its full note_meta scan plus per-row JSON parsing INSIDE the with_read_conn closure, holding the single process-wide read_db Mutex for a duration its own comment measures at ~12 s cold — so every other read-path IPC in the app parks behind it.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: State: a 2 GB index on a cold boot (the exact condition the comment at template_discovery.rs:820-827 measured at ~12 s; warm 0.33 s). Action: the user clicks the Template Studio dock button (+layout.svelte:7906 -> TemplateStudio.svelte:158 invokes discover_template_shapes). Timing: with_read_conn (search.rs:1497) takes state.read_db.lock() and does not release it until the closure returns, i.e. after every note_meta row has been read and its properties_json/tags_json/headings_json parsed. For those ~12 s every other read command blocks on the same Mutex: get_backlink_rows (cache.rs:636), get_outgoing_rows (cache.rs:674), get_structural_children/ancestors/descendants (structural.rs:237/257/296), resolve_wikilink_cross_library (libraries.rs:2868) and — worst — the rename cascade's candidate seek in update_links_on_rename (libraries.rs:6688). Silent damage: the user opens a note or starts a rename during that window; backlinks/outgoing/structure panels never populate, a clicked wikilink does nothing, and the rename cascade stalls for up to 12 s with no error, no spinner on those surfaces and nothing in any log to attribute it — the app reads as hung. The (async) attribute added at line 828 fixed only the dispatch-thread half of this; the lock-hold half is untouched. The identical hazard was recognised and explicitly guarded in target_base_backfill.rs:154 ('with_read_conn holds read_db for the WHOLE closure ... would then block every other read at boot for seconds'), so the guard exists in the codebase and was simply not applied here.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified in code, not inferred. (1) search.rs:1492-1507 — with_read_conn holds the single process-wide state.read_db Mutex (search.rs:1353) for the ENTIRE closure. (2) template_discovery.rs:835-881 — discover_template_shapes puts an unbounded `SELECT path,name,library_name,properties_json,tags_json,headings_json FROM note_meta` (no WHERE/LIMIT) plus per-row JSON parsing inside that closure; only discover_shapes (line 883) runs outside it, so the cold cost the file's own comment measures (:821-824, "COLD it is ~12 s on a 2 GB index — measured", warm 0.33 s) is the in-lock portion. (3) Eight other read commands take the same mutex and are reachable during the hold: cache.rs:636 get_backlink_rows, cache.rs:674 get_outgoing_rows, structural.rs:237/257/296, libraries.rs:2868 resolve_wikilink_cross_library, and libraries.rs:6688 — the rename cascade's candidate seek + freshness map. (4) Reachable by an ordinary action: dock button +layout.svelte:7906 -> TemplateStudio.svelte:158 onMount invoke; the Studio is full-page but the sidebar stays live, and nothing cancels the Rust scan when the panel closes, so clicking a note or starting a rename inside the window parks those commands for the remainder of the hold. (5) The identical hazard is explicitly recognised and guarded in-repo at target_base_backfill.rs:154-161 ("with_read_conn holds read_db for the WHOLE closure ... would then block every other read at boot for seconds") — the guard exists and was simply not applied here. (6) Verified the (async) claim against the actual dependency: tauri 2.10.3 + tauri-macros 2.5.5 route a sync fn marked (async) through respond_async_serialized -> async_runtime::spawn on the multi-thread Tokio runtime (wrapper.rs:241, ipc/mod.rs:375, async_runtime.rs:213), so the body blocks a Tokio worker, NOT the WebView2 dispatch thread — the (async) fix addressed only the dispatch half, exactly as the candidate states, and the lock-hold half is untouched. Silence is real: the blocked surfaces surface no error, no spinner and write nothing to diagnostics.log; the user sees backlinks/outgoing/structure never populate, a clicked wikilink do nothing, and a rename stall. Partial refutation applied to severity, not to the finding: the stall is bounded and self-resolving (all blocked queries return correct results once the guard drops), there is no data loss, no index<->disk divergence and no leak; the triggering panel does show templateStudio.loading; and warm cost is 0.33 s, so the multi-second case is essentially once per cold boot on a large index. That rules out APP-KILLER/HIGH but not the defect itself — a multi-second, cue-less serialization of every read path including the rename cascade is the same class this codebase already ruled unacceptable (PJ-066 §C3; the 47 s scan_unlinked_mentions freeze; target_base_backfill §6g).

confirmed_findings.summary: linkMentionInNote writes a new [[wikilink]] into the note's BODY through the watcher-suppressed gate but never emits 'screen:note-saved', so a second screen showing that note keeps rendering the pre-link body indefinitely.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: Note B is open in a tab on the second screen (opened via 'Send to second screen' or a workspace restore). In the main window the user clicks 'link it' on an unlinked mention of A inside B. linkMentionInNote does writeNote(...,'link_mention') at store.ts:1643 — write_gate marks the path watcher-suppressed (write_gate.rs:256-257), so no 'library-changed' fires — then reloadTabsFromDisk for the MAIN window's own tab and reindexNote. No emit('screen:note-saved'). The SS's u2 adopt handler (SecondScreenPage.svelte:673) is the only channel that would have re-read disk for that path, and it never runs. The SS's NoteEditor and its noteModel keep the pre-link body as both display and baseline. No error, no banner, no cue; the SS shows a note body that no longer exists on disk until some unrelated save of B happens to broadcast.
confirmed_findings.reason: Mechanism verified in source, but the severity framing is downgraded. CONFIRMED part: linkMentionInNote (store.ts:1612-1673) mutates the note BODY at line 1643 through writeNote -> invoke('write_note'), and write_gate::atomic_write calls watcher_suppress::mark(&tmp) + mark_with_parent(path), so no 'library-changed' fires (TTL 2.5s covers the write). No Rust emit is reached either — libraries.rs emits 'cascade:rewrote' only from resolve_structural_conflict (:2535) and update_links_on_rename (:6909). The pre-write flushOpenTabOrAbort uses a bare standardSaveEnv with NO onSaved (contrast navFlushEnv at store.ts:1885, which does emit 'screen:note-saved'), and reloadTabsFromDisk emits nothing. The SS's only content channels are onNoteSaved/'screen:note-saved' (SecondScreenPage.svelte:673), 'cascade:rewrote' (:713) and 'library-changed' (:781); none fire, so adoptFreshDiskIntoSS never runs and the second screen silently keeps rendering the pre-link body — no error, no banner, no cue — until an unrelated broadcasting save, a universe switch, or an SS reopen. REFUTED part (the 'clobber' class): SecondScreenPage.svelte:208 sets `const ssReadOnly = true` and passes it to every NoteEditor mount (:1210/:1253/:1419), so no keystroke can dirty an SS model; setDisplayOnlyWindow() (:213) arms the PJ-130 guard at store.ts:688 where flushOutgoing returns {ok:true} without writing on every departure path. The stale SS model therefore can NEVER write back — disk and the main window remain correct, there is no source-of-truth divergence, no data loss, no index drift. What remains is a genuine but bounded defect: a silent on-screen-vs-disk divergence in a read-only auxiliary display. Same omission exists on addLinkToNote's 'reviewer_connect' write (store.ts:1562); fix both by adding emit('screen:note-saved', {path}) after the durable write, matching navFlushEnv.

confirmed_findings.summary: addTagToNote's CLOSED-note branch writes the tag through the gate and reindexes, but never emits 'screen:note-saved' — the sibling of the two store.ts sites, same missed cross-window notification.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: Note N is closed in the main window but open on the second screen (SS tabs are independent). Right-click → Add tag in main takes the closed-note branch: readNote → writeNote(...,'add_tag') at +layout.svelte:7079 → reindexNote. The gated write suppresses the watcher, and no broadcastNoteSaved / emit('screen:note-saved') is issued (contrast NoteEditor.svelte:266/320/352/441/453/584 and navFlushEnv store.ts:652, which all broadcast). The second screen's copy of N never adopts the tag; its tag chips and cockpit stay wrong with no error.
confirmed_findings.reason:
Real and silent, but display-only — severity downgraded from MED to LOW.

CONFIRMED facts (read, not inferred):
- +layout.svelte:7043-7093 (closed-note branch): readNote → isCascading guard → markRecentWrite → writeNote(...,'add_tag') → reindexNote → markOrgChartDirty. No emit('screen:note-saved') / broadcastNoteSaved anywhere in the branch. The OPEN branch does broadcast, via saveTabContent's runPostSave (store.ts:1868). Every other write path in the same file broadcasts (e.g. FocusPane save, +layout.svelte:1793 `if (secondScreenOpen) broadcastNoteSaved(savedPath)`).
- No alternate channel exists. write_note → write_gate::gate_write → watcher_suppress::mark_with_parent (write_gate.rs:256-257), process-wide, so watcher.rs:125's 'library-changed' never fires for this write; the SS's u5/u5b/u5c listeners never run. constellation_search_reindex emits nothing app-wide. So the SS's copy of N stays stale indefinitely with no error and no self-correction (only a universe switch, index-repair, or the note being opened+saved in main clears it).
- Reachability is real: SecondScreenPage.svelte:846 restores the SS's OWN workspace tabs and :1390 opens notes from the SS's own UI, independent of main's tab list — so 'closed in main, live on the SS' is an ordinary state.

What refutes the MED severity (write-back hazard is structurally absent):
- The disk write is awaited and durable (gate_write = serialized + atomic + journaled); reindexNote surfaces its own failure via indexHealthError. The source of truth and the index are both CORRECT.
- The SS cannot write the stale copy back: SecondScreenPage.svelte:208 `const ssReadOnly = true`, passed to every NoteEditor mount (:1253, :1419), and NoteEditor.handleSave/handleFlush both early-return on readOnly (NoteEditor.svelte:361). The PJ-090 SS-clobber shape cannot occur.
- It cannot leak via the shared write-ahead net either: the readOnly return sits ABOVE setWriteAhead, and resolveNoteContent's staleSnapshot guard (store.ts:3145) rejects a snapshot whose bytes no longer match disk and prefers disk.

So the defect is a silent cross-window DISPLAY staleness (SS editor mount, cockpit editorPanelsData.content, tag chips show N without the tag), not silent data loss, index↔disk divergence, corruption, freeze, or leak. Fix is the one-line sibling broadcast; per the Whole-Ecosystem Fix Law, addLinkToNote's closed-note branch in the same file carries the identical omission and must be fixed in the same pass.

confirmed_findings.summary: retrySaveFailure's onSaved omits the 'screen:note-saved' broadcast that every other save site carries, so a save that only lands on the ~10 s auto-retry is never adopted by the second screen.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: User edits note N in the main window while N is also open on the second screen. The debounced save fails (file locked by AV/sync) — the save-health banner appears, the model stays dirty, the net is retained. ~10 s later the $effect retry timer (+layout.svelte:1762) calls retrySaveFailure, which saves through standardSaveEnv with onSaved = reindexNote ONLY (store.ts:524-531). standardSaveEnv itself does not broadcast (store.ts:503-506), and the gated write suppresses the watcher, so neither the SS's u2 ('screen:note-saved') nor u5 ('library-changed') handler fires. The write is now durable on disk and in the index, the banner clears, and the second screen still displays the pre-edit body — the one window that reports 'all good' is the one showing the wrong text.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified at the site: retrySaveFailure (store.ts:520-531) passes onSaved = reindexNote only; standardSaveEnv (store.ts:487-509) does not broadcast, so nothing upstream compensates. Every peer save site does broadcast (NoteEditor.svelte:318, store.ts:652 navFlushEnv, store.ts:1868 prop-save, store.ts:6166 merge_resolve), making this the lone outlier. The fallback channel is genuinely closed: gate_write marks watcher suppression (write_gate.rs:256-257, TTL 2.5s in watcher_suppress.rs:27) and the un-debounced notify watcher filters on was_recent (watcher.rs:118), so no 'library-changed' reaches the SS's u5 handler either. The 10s auto-retry $effect (+layout.svelte:1761-1767) makes the path routinely reachable: save fails on an AV/sync lock, the user stops typing, the retry lands durably, the banner clears — and the SS's u2 adopt (SecondScreenPage.svelte:673-709, the only content-refresh channel for an open SS note view) never fires. Result is a silent stale display in the companion window with the main window reporting success. Severity is bounded to LOW, not MED, because the SS is read-only by construction (ssReadOnly = true at SecondScreenPage.svelte:208, enforced by the readOnly early-returns in NoteEditor.svelte:285 and :208): the stale model can never be composed back over disk, so there is no cross-window clobber, no data loss, and no index divergence from this omission (reindexNote does run). It is a stale read-only view that corrects on the next ordinary save, cascade, or reopen. Note the separate and more serious sibling in the same onSaved — the missing reembedNote, which per store.ts:4128-4141 has no self-correcting path anywhere.

confirmed_findings.summary: KindRegistry::save() persists the custom-kind registry with `let _ = fs::write(path, json)` — non-atomic truncate-then-write AND the I/O error discarded; it is the one persisted-JSON writer in the app that never got crate::universe::atomic_write.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: Two failures, both silent. (a) Error discarded: the .constellation directory is read-only / the file is locked by a sync client when auto_generate fires during Canonicalize; the write fails, `let _ =` throws the error away, canonicalize_execute returns Ok with a full rename report, and the new kind code exists only in the in-process HashMap — the next run re-derives it and can pick a different code for the same extension than the one already written into the file names on disk. (b) Non-atomic: the app is killed (or loses power) between the truncate and the flush — every other persisted file in the app is protected from exactly this by atomic_write (temp + sync_all + rename, universe.rs:186) — leaving a half-JSON file_kinds.json. On the next construction, line 98's `unwrap_or_default()` reads that partial file as 'no custom kinds', and the first auto_generate overwrites it with one entry. The truncation caused by (b) is what makes finding #1 deterministic rather than luck-dependent.
confirmed_findings.reason: The mechanism is real and verified at the site, but the severity is overstated. CONFIRMED as a genuine silent defect: file_kinds.rs:181-190 `save()` is `let _ = fs::write(path, json)` — the I/O error is discarded with no return value, no log, no propagation, and `auto_generate` (line 176) returns the code and `import_with_canonical` returns a success ImportResult regardless. It is also the only persisted-JSON writer that bypasses `crate::universe::atomic_write` (universe.rs:186), whose own doc-comment asserts that every persisted-state file goes through it — so a kill/power-loss mid-write leaves a partial file that loader line 98 (`serde_json::from_str(...).unwrap_or_default()`) silently reads as "no custom kinds" and the next auto_generate overwrites. None of the refutation conditions apply: the write is not awaited/durable, the error is surfaced nowhere, there is no guard/version-gate/reconcile, and the path IS reachable (ImporterModal.svelte:65 -> import_with_canonical, importers.rs:828-831 builds the registry with a real config path, and collect_source_files_recursive at importers.rs:990-1009 collects ALL files not just .md, so Layer 3 auto_generate fires on any unknown extension). Downgraded MED -> LOW because the blast radius is far smaller than claimed: (1) code derivation is deterministic per extension (base = first 6 chars uppercased; the collision branch only fires when has_code(base) is already true), so a lost registry re-derives the SAME code — divergence requires two distinct unknown extensions sharing a 6-char prefix imported in a different order in a later session; (2) nothing ever reads the mapping back — I grepped canonical.rs and the kind is only ever WRITTEN (frontmatter at 215/336/380/621/664, stem at generate_canonical 49-93), while is_canonical_filename (1270-1287) validates only the timestamp shape and ignores the kind, and no command exposes custom_kinds to the frontend; (3) no overwrite risk, since generate_canonical probes `dir.join(&full).exists()` and re-rolls the random suffix; (4) the actual note writes on that path are gated and error-collected (write_gate::gate_write, result.errors). So what is silently lost or truncated is a registry of auto-generated cosmetic labels with no consumer — not note content, not the index, not earned link/review state. Real, silent, worth fixing (route through universe::atomic_write and propagate/log the error), but not MED and nowhere near app-killer.

confirmed_findings.summary: persistWorkspaces() is fire-and-forget with no single-flight chain, so two overlapping saves of workspaces.json can land out of order and the older list wins on disk — the precise race the sibling saveCollections was rewritten to prevent (store.ts:2142-2176, '★ Inspection 2026-07-29 — saves are SINGLE-FLIGHT').
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: The user deletes two saved layouts from the workspaces list in quick succession. deleteWorkspace(X) updates the store and invokes save_universe_workspaces with [A,B,Y]; before that IPC resolves, deleteWorkspace(Y) invokes with [A,B]. save_universe_workspaces is #[tauri::command(async)], so the two run concurrently on Tokio workers and each does its own atomic_write; if the first rename commits last, workspaces.json ends as [A,B,Y]. The UI shows both deletions applied, no error is raised anywhere, and Y silently reappears at the next boot or universe switch. workspaces.json has no .prev rotation and no second copy, so nothing reconciles it. Same window applies to a Save-workspace click racing a delete, where the surviving write drops the newly saved layout instead.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified in code, not inferred. persistWorkspaces (src/lib/libraries/store.ts:7680-7692) snapshots get(workspaces) at call time and fires invoke() with .then/.catch only — no chain, no in-flight guard; the workspacesLoaded gate covers only the read-failure class. The sibling saveCollections in the SAME file (lines 2142-2176) was explicitly rewritten to be single-flight for this exact hazard ('★ Inspection 2026-07-29 — saves are SINGLE-FLIGHT, and each reads the store at ITS turn'); the workspaces writer never got it. Concurrency is real on the Rust side: save_universe_workspaces (src-tauri/src/universe.rs:1760) is #[tauri::command(async)] over a sync body, which tauri-macros-2.5.5 wrapper.rs routes as 'sync_threadpool' → body_async → respond_async_serialized → tauri-2.10.3/src/ipc/mod.rs:375 crate::async_runtime::spawn — each invoke is an independent task on the multi-threaded runtime, with nothing serializing two invocations. atomic_write (universe.rs:186) uses a unique temp name per write (PJ-187), so there is no torn file — which is precisely why the outcome is plain last-rename-wins; the reorder window is the create+write_all+sync_all span, which the function's own comment puts at '100ms–seconds on network/USB/AV-scanned disks', and each write creates a fresh file that AV scans anew. Reachability is concrete: WorkspaceManager.svelte:34-35 and :81 expose a per-row '×' delete with no confirm, no disable, no await, so two clicks land two invokes milliseconds apart; the `saving` flag guards only save-vs-save, not save-vs-delete. Nothing reconciles: unlike session.json (session_rotate_once/.prev), workspaces.json has no rotation and no second copy, read_universe_workspaces just reads the file, and both writes return Ok so workspacesError stays null — no error is surfaced anywhere. The in-memory store stays correct, so the divergence is invisible until the next boot or universe switch, where the deleted layout reappears (or, in the delete-then-save reorder, the newly saved layout is gone). The only mitigation is incidental — a later saveWorkspace/deleteWorkspace rewrites the whole list from the correct store — which is luck, not a guard.

confirmed_findings.summary: When `rewrite_frontmatter_sources` / `rewrite_frontmatter_content_type` take their 'malformed frontmatter — leave alone' early return (mod.rs:551-552, 1160-1161), the caller still reports the requested IDs as `effective`, mirrors them into `note_meta`, clears the suggestion row and returns Ok — nothing landed on disk.
confirmed_findings.silent_failure_scenario: `rewrite_note_sources_on_disk` computes `effective = recognised(&ids, is_valid_source_id)` (mod.rs:728) from the REQUESTED ids, never from `rewritten`, and unconditionally returns `Ok(Some(rewritten))` to `gate_rmw`; the content_type twin does the same with `effective = ids` (mod.rs:1247). Both writers return `content.to_string()` unchanged when `rest[3..].find("\n---")` is None — a note whose opening `---` fence is never closed (truncated/partially-synced file, an imported `.md` that opens with a `---` thematic rule, a note left unterminated by an external editor). Sequence: user Accepts that note's card in Source Review → `sources_set_manual` writes nothing to disk but returns Ok, `write_sources_to_db` sets `note_meta.sources = ["testimony"]`, `clear_suggestions` deletes the row, the panel filters the card away, and `content_type_set_manual` (mod.rs:1330) additionally clears the row. `announce_frontmatter_write` then fires `library-changed`, the frontend queues a reindex, and `index_note`'s UPSERT (search.rs:8182-8183, `sources = excluded.sources`) re-derives from the untouched file and overwrites `note_meta.sources` back to NULL. Net: the user's classification is silently discarded with no error, and the same note re-enters the queue and fails identically every time. `bulk_ops::accept_one` has the same shape at bulk_ops.rs:453-468 — `after_both == content` yields `Ok(None)`/`wrote=false`, yet `mirror_to_db` still writes `merged_h`/`merged_v` and clears the row, so Approve-All drops such a note from the queue having written nothing. Measured on the Boss's test Universe (7,966 notes): 0 files currently in this shape, so the path is conditional today — but the writer has no way to tell its caller it declined, so the day one such note exists the failure is completely silent.
confirmed_findings.reason: Verified end-to-end in the actual source; every refutation route was attempted and failed. (1) `rewrite_frontmatter_sources` (src-tauri/src/sources/mod.rs:550-553) returns `content.to_string()` verbatim when `fence_offset` finds a leading `---` but `rest[3..].find(\"\\n---\")` is None; the content_type twin does the same at mod.rs:1160-1161. (2) `rewrite_note_sources_on_disk` (mod.rs:718-731) still hands `gate_rmw` `Ok(Some(rewritten))`, and `write_gate::gate_rmw` (write_gate.rs:662-680) only short-circuits on `None` — so it atomic-writes byte-identical content, journals `WriteOutcome::Ok` and returns Ok. Line 728 then sets `effective = recognised(&ids, is_valid_source_id)` from the REQUESTED ids, never from `rewritten`; the content_type twin sets `effective = ids` at mod.rs:1247. (3) `sources_set_manual` mirrors that set into `note_meta.sources` and DELETEs the suggestion row (mod.rs:828-829) and returns Ok; `content_type_set_manual` does the same at mod.rs:1314/1326. No error is raised on any layer, so the panel's catch never fires and the card leaves the queue. (4) The divergence then resolves in the WRONG direction with no message: `announce_frontmatter_write` emits `library-changed` with `libraryId: ''`, which +layout.svelte:3736-3759 treats as an announce and unconditionally adds the path to `pendingReindex`; `index_note`'s UPSERT sets `sources = excluded.sources` / `content_type = excluded.content_type` (search.rs NOTE_META_UPSERT) re-derived from the untouched file, zeroing the column. The user's Accept evaporates silently. (5) `bulk_ops::accept_one` is the sharpest form: its closure correctly returns `Ok(None)` for the no-op and the code even computes `let wrote = matches!(outcome, WriteOutcome::Ok)` (bulk_ops.rs:463), then calls `mirror_to_db` at line 468 regardless of `wrote` — writing `merged_h`/`merged_v` and clearing the suggestion row for a write it KNOWS did not happen; and because `announce` is correctly gated on `wrote`, no reindex is scheduled, so that mirror divergence persists indefinitely. Refutations rejected: the write is awaited/durable but writes unchanged bytes; no error is surfaced anywhere; the only existing guard (gate_rmw's `None`) is never reached by the two per-card writers and is deliberately bypassed by bulk_ops' mirror; the PJ-207 reconcile drift check compares files to index rows and cannot see a derived column stale against itself; and it does not self-correct visibly. NOT an app-killer: no `.md` content is lost or corrupted (the file is untouched) — what is lost is one classification act plus a regenerable suggestion row. Severity downgraded MED → LOW on measured evidence, not mechanism: the trigger requires a note whose first line is `---` with no later line-initial `---` (a leading thematic rule, or an unterminated/truncated frontmatter block), and the prior whole-app sweep's full-file scan of 20,236 .md files across E:\\Constellation Universes found ZERO notes in that shape (my own re-scan of the 7,966-note test universe was still running at timeout and was stopped). Reachable-in-principle, not live today. Fix is one line at each of three sites: return `Ok(None)` when the rewrite produced no change, and gate the DB mirror + `clear_suggestions` on the write having actually happened.
